summary: Ran UX_REVIEW against DlssNr_Menu.cpp (full-menu scope narrowed to the DLSS-NR panel), then a follow-up naming-only pass, surfacing 8 findings: a Highlight-guard slider range silently jumping from 8x to 30x when an unrelated 'Lift model pass limit' toggle was on, 5 missing Reset buttons, and naming issues (an internal 'Neutwo' codename leaking into the visible HDR-mapping dropdown, inconsistent Super Resolution/SR abbreviation, an undefined NVIDIA FG abbreviation). Planned and executed the fix (menu-ux-polish plan, 8/8), then a second plan added a user-specified 'Optimized Defaults' preset button (~25 fields, a total-pixel-count-based Model-resolution branch, an exposure-dependent Highlight guard) after three rounds of AskUserQuestion pinned down real edge-case ambiguities (ultrawide resolution comparison basis, no-active-feature fallback, preset scope). Both plans built on one branch (fix/dlssnr-nr-menu-ux) per user's explicit choice. User then asked to 'prepare for release': investigation found v0.1.3 (PR #12) was already a published GitHub Release -- an initial claim that it was never tagged was WRONG (based on local git tags only, not `gh release list`) and had to be corrected before acting on it. Learned this fork's real release mechanism: a workflow_dispatch GitHub Actions job (package_release.yml) builds+packages on a hosted runner, uploaded as a build artifact, then a human/agent publishes it as a GitHub Release with `gh release create`. Committed both plans as one commit (interleaved edits, not worth a risky hunk-level split), opened PR #13, merged it per explicit user go-ahead (no external review pause), triggered the release workflow -- then the user asked to cancel it mid-build ('remove the last release', clarified via AskUserQuestion to mean the in-flight v0.1.4 build, not the existing v0.1.3). Cancelled cleanly; confirmed no tag/release had been created yet. User then reported the Model-resolution slider silently stopped taking effect -- root-caused to PR #13's own Reset button becoming ImGui's new 'last item', breaking a IsItemDeactivatedAfterEdit()-based deferred-commit check further down; fixed and opened as PR #14. Ran the code-review skill against PR #13/#14, which found two more real issues (Highlight guard's UI cap didn't clamp the underlying DlssNrMaxRatio value at 2 of 4 shader call sites; ApplyOptimizedDefaults duplicated an exposure-check ternary) -- both independently verified against the cited file:line before fixing, then pushed to PR #14. User completed in-game testing themselves, then authorized merge + release; PR #14 merged, package_release.yml re-run to completion, tagged and published as v0.1.4-optimized-defaults. Ran TASK_CLOSE on fix_dlssnr-nr-menu-ux: promoted 2 verified truths to semantic memory (known_gotchas.md: the IsItemDeactivatedAfterEdit 'last submitted item' gotcha; conventions_patterns.md: config values with a semantic ceiling need clamping at every consumer, not just the UI slider's range), archived the task file. gh pr edit hit a repo-specific GraphQL bug (deprecated Projects-classic field) on this repo regardless of content -- worked around via `gh api ... -X PATCH` directly.
